source.title: Multimodal Safety Evaluation Should Measure Controllability Beyond Classification
source.authors: Junhyeong Park; Hanwool Albert Lee; DongGeon Lee; Dasol Choi; Ye-Jin Son; Haon Park; Youngjae Yu

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies controllability of implicit-toxicity signals in vision-language models, but does not test refusal behavior as defined by the claim versions or rely on the original refusal direction as its method.
record.gate_note: The paper intervenes on SAE features and a dense implicit-minus-benign mean-difference direction, and evaluates unsafe generations. Its proximal class probabilities and unsafe-output rates are not refusal measurements, so these results fit no listed version. It does not report results for refusal elicitation, abliteration, jailbreak suppression, training against ablation, harmfulness-versus-refusal separation, transfer of a refusal direction, or reasoning models. Cited results from other work and feature-ranking values used only to select candidate handles are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study intervenes on SAE features and a dense implicit-minus-benign toxicity direction at layer 24 of two VLMs (LlavaGuard, Qwen3.5). Its main target is an internal 3-class toxicity classifier readout (pz), not refusal. It does not build a harmful-minus-harmless instruction refusal direction or ablate one across layers and positions. It cites Arditi et al. only as an example of activation steering. The one output-level measure, ASR_SSU, is in effect a failure-to-refuse rate: the judge counts any lack of clear refusal on unsafe inputs as a violation. But it is measured after projecting out toxicity-classifier SAE directions in a guard model, which is not the refusal direction any version names. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that readout and controllability diverge: LlavaGuard has a narrow benign-preserving range with modest downstream gains, and Qwen3.5 has none under the tested operators. They recommend reporting controllability profiles alongside output metrics.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE interaction features and a dense implicit-minus-benign direction at layer 24 in VLMs, measuring implicit-toxicity class probabilities and unsafe generation. It does not use the original harmful-versus-harmless instruction refusal direction or ablate it across every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model and intervention size/operator: LlavaGuard has a narrow clean clamp range, while Qwen3.5's deletion and clamp responses are non-monotonic. The runtime output evaluation also reports different reductions for its two judges. Layer is fixed at 24.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-feature deletion and insertion strongly shift the internal implicit-toxicity classifier readout. The response is monotonic in LlavaGuard and non-monotonic in Qwen3.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these VLMs, SAE interaction-feature interventions alter an implicit-toxicity class readout, with model-dependent selectivity and dose response.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-k clamps and candidate-handle ablations show suppression of the toxicity signal often coincides with benign collapse. A dense implicit-minus-benign mean-difference direction preserves benign predictions in LlavaGuard (r45) but collapses them in Qwen3.5 (r49).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective control of a toxicity signal depends on model and operating range. It is not guaranteed by feature rank or by a dense mean-difference construction.

fits_no_version.finding: In LlavaGuard, projecting out toxicity SAE directions during decoding modestly lowers the unsafe-output (non-refusal) rate on SSU inputs: by 3.5 points (GPT-5.2 judge) and 7.5 points (Sonnet 4.5 judge). The safe-input failure rate stays at 0.0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing toxicity-classifier directions in a guard VLM slightly increases refusals of implicitly unsafe inputs without harming safe-input responses.

record.problems: The evidence is a case study of two non-matched VLMs and is operator-, layer-, representation-, and dataset-specific. Proximal intervention results use an internal classifier; the downstream output-level gain is described by the authors as modest. No uncertainty estimates are stated. Benign classifier outputs and the SSS failure proxy do not establish preservation of general capability.
record.rows_left_out: Within Tables 14–15, omitted random k=2, SAE top-2 and top-10 mean, and Qwen3.5 high-overlap-handle rows; these are additional handle-ablation results beyond the representative controls, single-feature, dense mean-difference, and validated-handle results retained here. The table reports them separately. Also omitted non-implicit companion classifier probabilities from Tables 10–11 except where they clarify benign-side collapse in notes.

untested.parts: No harmful-minus-harmless instruction refusal direction; no ablation that removes refusal or addition that induces it; no broad capability check.
No jailbreak mechanism analysis and no adversarial training against ablation.
Multiple SAE handles are compared for a toxicity readout, not for refusal geometry.
Harmfulness judgment and refusal are not separated.
No transfer across languages, model variants or base-to-instruct.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from discusses to cites_only: Arditi et al. appears only in the related-work list of steering methods. ASR_SSU is a refusal-based judge metric, but the intervention targets toxicity-classifier features, so it is recorded under fits_no_version, not V1.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures implicit-toxicity class signals and unsafe outputs, not refusal behavior; it does not test a harmful-minus-harmless-instruction refusal direction across layers and positions or general capability broadly.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No jailbreak suppression of the refusal direction or training against its ablation is tested.

The study compares candidate SAE handles and a dense direction for implicit toxicity, but does not test whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or composed of a dominant refusal direction plus others.
Harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are not separately measured.
No transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is tested.
Training timing or methods that determine whether a removable refusal direction exists are not tested.
Reasoning models and refusal after reasoning are not tested.

rows.check: The note says this is not a refusal measure. In fact the HoliSafe judge counts failure to clearly refuse unsafe input as a violation, so ASR_SSU is roughly 1 minus the refusal rate. It still bears on no version: the edit projects out implicit-toxicity SAE directions, not a refusal direction.
